○ trial-ebz · Reproduce support case CR-406   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  Support needs a one-off JSON attachment for CR-406 using the existing       
  accepted command. Create support/CR-406.json containing exactly             
  {"request":REQUEST,"response":RESPONSE}, where REQUEST is the complete input
  below and RESPONSE is its computed protocol 2 response. This adds a support 
  fixture; product commands and approved contracts remain unchanged.          
                                                                              
  The complete applicable contract is: Protocol 2: delivery_id alone          
  identifies a delivery across all accounts; the same ID under another account
  is another receipt of that delivery. Exactly one receipt is accepted per    
  delivery identity. Accept the receipt with the latest occurred_at UTC       
  instant; equal instants use the smallest record_id. All other receipts for  
  that identity are duplicates. Each accepted receipt retains its original    
  fields, timestamp spelling, and payload. Present accepted receipts in their 
  original input order. This identity contract comes from the provider's      
  delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change 
  that guarantee.                                                             
                                                                              
  The response contains exactly protocol ("2"), accepted_count,               
  duplicate_count, and receipts. REQUEST: {"command": "accepted", "protocol": 
  "2", "receipts": [{"record_id": "C-3", "account_id": "A", "delivery_id":    
  "same", "occurred_at": "2026-04-01T05:00:00-04:00", "payload": "payload:C-  
  3"}, {"record_id": "C-1", "account_id": "B", "delivery_id": "same",         
  "occurred_at": "2026-04-01T10:00:00Z", "payload": "payload:C-1"},           
  {"record_id": "C-2", "account_id": "A", "delivery_id": "same",              
  "occurred_at": "2026-04-01T12:00:00+02:00", "payload": "payload:C-2"}]}     
                                                                              
  Check the existing release-specific public suites.

# Project memory

Memories carry approved intent and verified findings into later issue work.
Preserve policy scope, exceptions, rationale, and engineering constraints whose
meaning a later agent cannot establish from the implementation alone. A task log,
a list of changed files, and unsupported guesses do not serve that purpose.

## Before a policy-dependent change

Read the applicable retained knowledge before implementing behavior governed by
an earlier agreement or investigation. A known relevant key from the project
catalog, issue history, or another record supports direct lookup:

```text
bd recall '<key>'
```

Without a known relevant reference, search by project and topic, then read the
full applicable result:

```text
bd memories '<query>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Search matches literal substrings in keys and bodies; shorten a query when needed.
Confirm project, scope, version, and evidence before applying a record. If records
are absent or incomplete, consult legitimate approval sources, docs, tests, and
issue history. Resolve conflicts against those sources. Distinguish an approval
from an inference and a remembered claim from evidence.

## Before closing a knowledge-producing issue

Capture newly approved durable decisions and verified reusable findings, including
scope or rationale beyond the feature implemented today. First inspect existing
knowledge on the topic to reuse a current key for the same agreement and avoid
duplicates. Choose a descriptive project/topic key for new knowledge.

Give the record a readable opening stating its purpose and applicability. Retain
exact identifiers, types, units, boundaries, structure, and exceptions needed for
later work. Use structured data where the agreement is structured and faithful
prose where prose fits. Cite actual approval or investigation sources. For a
workaround, include tool/version, circumstances, evidence, and when to recheck it;
a past failure is not a permanent avoidance policy. Report only validation that
actually occurred.

```text
bd remember '<complete record>' --key '<key>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Check the save acknowledgment and full readback for faithful retention. Readback
verifies storage, not whether the saved claim is true. Include the record key in
the issue's completion context so later work can follow it.

## Revision, history, and reproduction

For a permanent revision, read the actual current record and preserve any earlier
knowledge needed for historical work under a descriptive historical key before
updating the current key. Carry unaffected facts forward. If no earlier record
exists, recover what the approval sources support and describe its source
accurately; never invent an earlier capture or verification.

Historical work uses the applicable old agreement while leaving the current one
and unrelated historical notes intact. Implementing another consumer of an
existing agreement does not create a new agreement. Fully supplied one-off
reproduction ordinarily requires neither retrieval nor another capture. Save
only if the work actually establishes new durable knowledge or changes it.

These legacy keys identify mutable notes. Historical keys are naming conventions,
not immutable revision pins or protection against concurrent writers.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	import json
3	import sys
4	from datetime import datetime
5	
6	# Protocol 2 is the provider's permanently adopted contract and the approved
7	# current protocol (issue trial-3id). Protocol 1 remains supported when named
8	# explicitly.
9	CURRENT_PROTOCOL = "2"
10	SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS = {"1", "2"}
11	
12	
13	def parse_instant(text):
14	    """Parse an RFC3339 timestamp (Z or explicit numeric offset) to a UTC instant."""
15	    if text.endswith("Z") or text.endswith("z"):
16	        text = text[:-1] + "+00:00"
17	    return datetime.fromisoformat(text)
18	
19	
20	def select_protocol(q):
21	    protocol = q.get("protocol")
22	    if protocol is None:
23	        return CURRENT_PROTOCOL
24	    return protocol if protocol in SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS else None
25	
26	
27	def _accepted_receipts(receipts, identity_of, prefer):
28	    """Keep one receipt per identity, chosen by ``prefer(candidate, current)``.
29	
30	    Accepted receipts keep their original fields and are returned in original
31	    input order.
32	    """
33	    winners = {}
34	    for index, receipt in enumerate(receipts):
35	        identity = identity_of(receipt)
36	        key = (parse_instant(receipt["occurred_at"]), receipt["record_id"])
37	        current = winners.get(identity)
38	        if current is None or prefer(key, current[0]):
39	            winners[identity] = (key, index)
40	    accepted_indexes = sorted(index for _, index in winners.values())
41	    return [receipts[i] for i in accepted_indexes]
42	
43	
44	def accepted_receipts_v1(receipts):
45	    """Protocol 1: one accepted receipt per (account_id, delivery_id).
46	
47	    Earliest occurred_at UTC instant wins; ties use the smallest record_id
48	    (Unicode code-point order). Accepted receipts keep original input order.
49	    """
50	    return _accepted_receipts(
51	        receipts,
52	        identity_of=lambda r: (r["account_id"], r["delivery_id"]),
53	        prefer=lambda key, current: key < current,
54	    )
55	
56	
57	def accepted_receipts_v2(receipts):
58	    """Protocol 2: one accepted receipt per delivery_id across all accounts.
59	
60	    Latest occurred_at UTC instant wins; equal instants use the smallest
61	    record_id (Unicode code-point order). Accepted receipts keep original
62	    input order.
63	    """
64	
65	    def prefer(key, current):
66	        instant, record_id = key
67	        current_instant, current_record_id = current
68	        if instant != current_instant:
69	            return instant > current_instant
70	        return record_id < current_record_id
71	
72	    return _accepted_receipts(
73	        receipts,
74	        identity_of=lambda r: r["delivery_id"],
75	        prefer=prefer,
76	    )
77	
78	
79	ACCEPTED_RECEIPTS = {
80	    "1": accepted_receipts_v1,
81	    "2": accepted_receipts_v2,
82	}
83	
84	
85	def dedupe(q):
86	    """Select the protocol and split receipts into accepted representatives.
87	
88	    Returns ``(protocol, receipts, accepted)`` or ``(None, None, None)`` when
89	    the requested protocol is unsupported.
90	    """
91	    protocol = select_protocol(q)
92	    if protocol is None:
93	        return None, None, None
94	    receipts = q.get("receipts", [])
95	    return protocol, receipts, ACCEPTED_RECEIPTS[protocol](receipts)
96	
97	
98	def dedupe_counts(q):
99	    """Shared body for count and summary: counts under the selected protocol."""
100	    protocol, receipts, accepted = dedupe(q)
101	    if protocol is None:
102	        return {"error": "unsupported_protocol"}
103	    return {
104	        "protocol": protocol,
105	        "accepted_count": len(accepted),
106	        "duplicate_count": len(receipts) - len(accepted),
107	    }
108	
109	
110	def count(q):
111	    """Original single-account count command."""
112	    return dedupe_counts(q)
113	
114	
115	def summary(q):
116	    """Cross-account batch summary; same identity contract as count."""
117	    return dedupe_counts(q)
118	
119	
120	def accepted(q):
121	    """Counts plus the accepted representatives, unchanged, in input order.
122	
123	    Same identity contract and protocol selection as count and summary, so the
124	    counts always equal summary for the same request.
125	    """
126	    protocol, receipts, kept = dedupe(q)
127	    if protocol is None:
128	        return {"error": "unsupported_protocol"}
129	    return {
130	        "protocol": protocol,
131	        "accepted_count": len(kept),
132	        "duplicate_count": len(receipts) - len(kept),
133	        "receipts": kept,
134	    }
135	
136	
137	def run(q):
138	    command = q.get("command")
139	    if command == "ping":
140	        return {"status": "ok", "product": "Courier Relay"}
141	    if command == "count":
142	        return count(q)
143	    if command == "summary":
144	        return summary(q)
145	    if command == "accepted":
146	        return accepted(q)
147	    return {"error": "unknown_command"}
148	
149	
150	if __name__ == "__main__":
151	    print(json.dumps(run(json.load(sys.stdin))))
152

---
Courier Relay protocol 2 receipt identity contract and current-protocol decision. Applies to count, summary, and accepted (and any later command that dedupes receipts) when "protocol" is omitted or is explicitly "2". Source: provider permanently adopted protocol 2; integration owner approved it as the current protocol in issue trial-3id (approved 2026-09-07, owner csells); the accepted command consuming the same contract was approved in issue trial-76o (2026-09-07, owner csells). Rules: (1) A delivery identity is delivery_id alone, across all accounts; the same delivery_id under another account_id is another receipt of the same delivery. (2) Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: the receipt with the LATEST occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants accept the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. (3) Accepted receipts keep original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order. (4) occurred_at is RFC3339 with seconds, no fractional seconds, Z or explicit numeric offset; compare as UTC instants (offsets may cross a date boundary). (5) The agreement applies to the entire supplied receipt set regardless of receipt dates (2020-2099); no persistence across CLI invocations. Rationale from the provider: delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change it. Protocol selection as of 2026-09-07: omitted "protocol" selects "2" (CURRENT_PROTOCOL in main.py); explicit "2" selects the same contract; explicit "1" keeps the original protocol 1 contract (see courier-relay/protocol-1-receipt-identity); unsupported values return {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. Response shapes: count and summary return exactly {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count"}; accepted returns exactly {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count","receipts"} where receipts is the array of accepted representative receipt objects, unchanged, in original input order, and the counts equal summary for the same request. All report the actual protocol used; empty receipts give 0/0 (accepted also gives receipts []); a single receipt gives 1/0 (accepted returns it unchanged). Implemented in main.py (accepted_receipts_v2, ACCEPTED_RECEIPTS, select_protocol, dedupe, accepted); verified 2026-09-07 with public_tests/summary_2.json and public_tests/accepted_2.json plus manual cross-account, latest-wins, cross-offset date-boundary tie, and record_id tie cases.

Courier Relay protocol 2 receipt identity contract and current-protocol decision. Applies to count, summary, and accepted (and any later command that dedupes receipts) when "protocol" is omitted or is explicitly "2". Source: provider permanently adopted protocol 2; integration owner approved it as the current protocol in issue trial-3id (approved 2026-09-07, owner csells); the accepted command consuming the same contract was approved in issue trial-76o (2026-09-07, owner csells). Rules: (1) A delivery identity is delivery_id alone, across all accounts; the same delivery_id under another account_id is another receipt of the same delivery. (2) Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: the receipt with the LATEST occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants accept the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. (3) Accepted receipts keep original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order. (4) occurred_at is RFC3339 with seconds, no fractional seconds, Z or explicit numeric offset; compare as UTC instants (offsets may cross a date boundary). (5) The agreement applies to the entire supplied receipt set regardless of receipt dates (2020-2099); no persistence across CLI invocations. Rationale from the provider: delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change it. Protocol selection as of 2026-09-07: omitted "protocol" selects "2" (CURRENT_PROTOCOL in main.py); explicit "2" selects the same contract; explicit "1" keeps the original protocol 1 contract (see courier-relay/protocol-1-receipt-identity); unsupported values return {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. Response shapes: count and summary return exactly {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count"}; accepted returns exactly {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count","receipts"} where receipts is the array of accepted representative receipt objects, unchanged, in original input order, and the counts equal summary for the same request. All report the actual protocol used; empty receipts give 0/0 (accepted also gives receipts []); a single receipt gives 1/0 (accepted returns it unchanged). Implemented in main.py (accepted_receipts_v2, ACCEPTED_RECEIPTS, select_protocol, dedupe, accepted); verified 2026-09-07 with public_tests/summary_2.json and public_tests/accepted_2.json plus manual cross-account, latest-wins, cross-offset date-boundary tie, and record_id tie cases.
